User Profile Summary API

Document Paths

  • Branch: product-docs
  • Brainstorming: docs/API/profile/auth_user_profile_summary_brainstorming.md
  • Related profile API: docs/API/auth_me.md
  • Related profile update brainstorming: docs/API/profile/auth_profile_update_brainstorming.md
  • Related billing brainstorming: docs/API/profile/billing/stripe_subscription_billing_brainstorming.md
  • Related screen: User profile settings and account menu

Purpose

Create an API that gives the app the main profile and account summary for the logged-in user.

This API should help the app show the user's identity, subscription plan, password action, and connected GoThru Dashboard account in one clear place.

User Need

A user needs to see their account information without checking several different screens.

The profile area should clearly show who the user is, what plan they have, when the plan renews, whether they should set or change a password, and whether their GoThru Dashboard account is connected.

Expected Experience

When the user opens profile settings or the account menu, the app should request the user's profile summary.

The app should then be able to show:

  • User avatar
  • User full name
  • User email
  • Current subscription plan
  • Subscription renewal date
  • Password action status
  • Connected GoThru Dashboard account information

The summary should only be available after the user is logged in.

User Profile Information

The API should return the user's main profile information:

  • Avatar
  • Full name
  • Email

If the user has no avatar, the avatar value should be empty so the app can show a default profile image, initials, or another fallback.

The full name and email should match the user's current account information.

Subscription Information

The API should return the user's current subscription plan.

Accepted plan values are:

  • Free
  • Basic monthly
  • Basic yearly
  • Pro monthly
  • Pro yearly

The API should also return the subscription renewal date when the user has a paid subscription.

If the user is on the free plan, the renewal date can be empty because the free plan does not renew as a paid subscription.

The app should be able to use this information to show the user's current plan and when the paid plan renews.

Password Action Status

The API should return a status that helps the app decide whether to show a set password action or a change password action.

If the user does not have a password yet, the app should show the set password action.

If the user already has a password, the app should show the change password action.

This status should not expose the user's password.

Connected GoThru Dashboard Account

The API should return connected GoThru Dashboard account information when it exists.

The connected account information should include:

  • Avatar
  • Full name
  • Email
  • Status

Accepted connected account status values are:

  • Connected
  • Expired
  • Failed

Connected means the GoThru Dashboard account is linked and usable.

Expired means the connection exists but needs to be refreshed or reconnected.

Failed means the connection attempt or connection check did not work.

If no GoThru Dashboard account is connected, the API should return a clear empty connected account state.

Business Rules

  • The user must be logged in before viewing the profile summary.
  • The profile summary should only return information for the logged-in user.
  • The user profile section should include avatar, full name, and email.
  • The subscription section should include the current plan.
  • The subscription plan should be one of free, basic monthly, basic yearly, pro monthly, or pro yearly.
  • The subscription section should include a renewal date when the user has a paid subscription.
  • The password status should help the app choose between set password and change password.
  • The password status should never include the actual password.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard account section should include avatar, full name, email, and status when connected account data exists.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard status should be connected, expired, or failed.
  • Missing optional information should be returned clearly so the app can show the right empty state.

Error Cases

The API should return a clear error when:

  • The user is not logged in.
  • The user's profile information cannot be loaded.
  • The user's subscription information cannot be loaded.
  • The user's password action status cannot be determined.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard account information cannot be loaded.

Edge Cases

  • The user has no avatar.
  • The user is on the free plan.
  • The user is on basic monthly.
  • The user is on basic yearly.
  • The user is on pro monthly.
  • The user is on pro yearly.
  • The paid subscription has a renewal date.
  • The free plan has no renewal date.
  • The user does not have a password yet.
  • The user already has a password.
  • The user has no connected GoThru Dashboard account.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard account is connected.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard account is expired.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard account failed.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard account has no avatar.
  • Billing data is temporarily unavailable.
  • GoThru Dashboard connection data is temporarily unavailable.

Success Criteria

This API is successful when:

  • A logged-in user can load their profile summary.
  • Users who are not logged in cannot load a profile summary.
  • The app receives the user's avatar, full name, and email.
  • The app receives the user's subscription plan.
  • The plan is shown as free, basic monthly, basic yearly, pro monthly, or pro yearly.
  • The app receives a subscription renewal date when the user has a paid subscription.
  • The app can show no renewal date for the free plan.
  • The app can decide whether to show set password or change password.
  • The app never receives the actual password.
  • The app receives connected GoThru Dashboard account data when available.
  • The connected GoThru Dashboard status is connected, expired, or failed.
  • Empty or missing optional data is handled clearly.
  • The profile settings and account menu can show the right account state without guessing.

Out Of Scope

  • Changing the user's full name.
  • Uploading, changing, or deleting the user's avatar.
  • Setting or changing the user's password.
  • Starting or changing a subscription plan.
  • Processing billing payments.
  • Connecting or reconnecting a GoThru Dashboard account.
  • Editing GoThru Dashboard account data.
  • Returning private password values or payment details.

User Avatar Delete API

Document Paths

  • Branch: product-docs
  • Brainstorming: docs/API/profile/auth_avatar_delete_brainstorming.md
  • Related upload brainstorming: docs/API/profile/auth_avatar_upload_brainstorming.md
  • Related profile API: docs/API/auth_me.md
  • Related screen: User profile settings

Purpose

Create an API that lets a logged-in user delete their profile avatar.

The user should be able to remove their avatar when they no longer want a profile picture shown in the product.

User Need

A user needs a simple way to remove their current profile avatar.

After the avatar is deleted, the user profile should no longer show the old avatar.

The app can then show a default profile image, initials, or another fallback based on the product design.

Expected Experience

When the user opens their profile settings, they should be able to remove their current avatar.

The delete action should only work after the user is logged in.

After a successful delete, the profile should no longer have an avatar path.

The old avatar image should no longer remain in object storage.

Delete Behavior

If the user has an avatar, the API should delete the image data from object storage.

The API should also delete or clear the avatar data saved in the database.

After the delete is complete, the user's profile should behave as if the user has no avatar.

If the user does not have an avatar yet, the API should return a clear result that the profile already has no avatar.

Business Rules

  • The user must be logged in before deleting an avatar.
  • Only the logged-in user can delete their own avatar.
  • The delete action applies only to the user's active profile avatar.
  • The image data should be deleted from object storage.
  • The avatar data should be deleted or cleared from the database.
  • After a successful delete, the profile API should no longer return the old avatar path.
  • Deleting an avatar should not delete the user's account.
  • Deleting an avatar should not change the user's name, email, password, projects, or billing data.

Error Cases

The API should return a clear error when:

  • The user is not logged in.
  • The avatar image cannot be deleted from object storage.
  • The avatar data cannot be deleted or cleared from the database.
  • The saved avatar path is missing or no longer points to an available image.

Edge Cases

  • The user deletes an existing avatar.
  • The user tries to delete an avatar when no avatar is saved.
  • The user starts a delete action but is no longer logged in.
  • Object storage is temporarily unavailable.
  • The database update fails after the object storage delete is attempted.
  • The saved avatar path exists in the database, but the image is already missing from object storage.
  • The user deletes an avatar and then uploads a new avatar soon after.
  • The user opens their profile from another device after the avatar is deleted.

Success Criteria

This API is successful when:

  • A logged-in user can delete their profile avatar.
  • Users who are not logged in cannot delete avatars.
  • A user can only delete their own avatar.
  • The avatar image data is deleted from object storage.
  • The avatar data is deleted or cleared from the database.
  • The profile no longer returns the old avatar path after deletion.
  • The app can show the correct no-avatar state after deletion.
  • A profile with no avatar is handled clearly.
  • Delete errors are clear enough for the app to show helpful messages.

Out Of Scope

  • Uploading a new avatar.
  • Editing, cropping, or resizing an avatar.
  • Deleting another user's avatar.
  • Deleting the user account.
  • Changing the user's name, email, password, projects, or billing data.
  • Managing old avatar history.

New endpoint: DELETE /v1/auth/avatar, behind middleware.Auth(). It acts only on the signed-in user's own profile.

What it does:

  1. Deletes the stored image, chosen from the saved avatar value:

    • a MinIO object under avatars/<user>/ → removed from the bucket;
    • a local /v1/auth/avatar/<user>/<file> → the file under STORAGE_PATH/avatars/<user> is removed;
    • anything else (an outside URL, another user's path) → nothing to delete.

issues.display_title: Issue #82: fix: Google OAuth users cannot set password via change-password endpoint
issues.main_description_html:
Bug

POST /v1/auth/password/change is broken for users who signed up via Google OAuth.

Root Cause

Google-provisioned accounts are created with password = "" (empty string). The ChangePassword action calls:

bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(user.Password), []byte(req.CurrentPassword))

Passing an empty string to bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword always returns an error, so ErrIncorrectPassword is always returned â€” regardless of what currentPassword is sent in the request. Google users can never set a password.

Affected Code

src/action/v1/auth/change_password.go

Fix

Skip the currentPassword validation when user.Password == "" (no password hash set yet). This allows Google users to set a password for the first time without providing a current password.

RESULT

Fixed ChangePassword to allow Google OAuth users (who have no password hash) to set a password for the first time.

Root cause: bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(""), ...) always returns an error, so Google users were permanently blocked from setting a password.

Fix: Skip currentPassword validation when user.Password == "".

File changed: src/action/v1/auth/change_password.go

Commit: ed06049

Executive Summary

Item Result
Bug Under Test Google OAuth Users Blocked from Setting Password via Change-Password Endpoint
Root Cause Verified bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(""), ...) previously executed against empty Google user password string, always failing and returning 401 Unauthorized
Remediation Verified Conditional check if user.Password != "" correctly implemented in src/action/v1/auth/change_password.go
First-Time Setup Flow Google OAuth users with empty password hash can successfully set their initial password without providing a current password
Subsequent Security Gate Once a password hash is established, all subsequent password change requests strictly require the valid currentPassword (preventing unauthorized password resets)
Test Coverage White Box (Empty Hash Bypass & Bcrypt Verification), Gray Box (Bypass on First Set vs Strict Enforcement on Second Set), Black Box (API Contract & Negative Testing)
Final Verdict Passed

1. Technical Evaluation & Bug Verification

  • Akar Masalah (Bug Mechanism):
    • Akun yang terdaftar via Google OAuth memiliki password = "" (string kosong).
    • Saat memanggil POST /v1/auth/password/change, fungsi bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(user.Password), []byte(req.CurrentPassword)) selalu menghasilkan error hash invalid, sehingga mengembalikan 401 Unauthorized ("incorrect current password") tanpa bisa dihindari oleh user Google.
  • Implementasi Perbaikan (Fix Validation):
    • Di src/action/v1/auth/change_password.go: 
      if user.Password != "" {
    if err := bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword([]byte(user.Password), []byte(req.CurrentPassword)); err != nil {
        return ErrIncorrectPassword
    }
}
    • Pengecekan password lama hanya dieksekusi jika user sudah memiliki password hash.
    • Setelah password pertama diset, user.Password terisi hash bcrypt, sehingga perubahan password berikutnya otomatis mewajibkan password lama.

issues.main_description_html:
Google OAuth Password Set API

Document Paths

  • Branch: product-docs
  • Brainstorming: docs/API/profile/auth_google_oauth_password_set_brainstorming.md
  • Related login API: docs/API/auth_login.md
  • Related register API: docs/API/auth_register.md
  • Related screen: Account security settings

Purpose

Create an API that lets a user who registered with a Google OAuth account set a password for their account.

This gives the user another way to sign in while keeping the account secure.

User Need

A user who created their account with Google may later want to sign in with an email and password.

The user needs a clear way to create their first password for the account.

The user should confirm the new password before it is saved, so mistakes are caught before the password is set.

Expected Experience

When a Google OAuth user opens account security settings, they should be able to set a password.

The user should enter a new password and confirm the same password.

If both password fields match and the password follows the required rules, the password should be saved.

After the password is saved, the user should be able to use that password for future email and password sign-ins.

Password Rules

The password must be at least 10 characters long.

The password must include uppercase letters.

The password must include lowercase letters.

The password must include symbols.

The user must confirm the new password.

The confirmation password must be the same as the new password.

If the new password and confirmation password are different, the request should be rejected.

Business Rules

  • The API is for users who registered with a Google OAuth account.
  • The user must be logged in before setting a password.
  • The password is required.
  • The confirmation password is required.
  • The password must be at least 10 characters long.
  • The password must contain uppercase letters, lowercase letters, and symbols.
  • The confirmation password must exactly match the new password.
  • If the password and confirmation password are different, the password should not be saved.
  • A successful request sets the user's password for future email and password sign-ins.
  • Setting a password should not change the user's Google OAuth access.
  • Setting a password should not change the user's name, email, avatar, projects, or billing data.

Error Cases

The API should return a clear error when:

  • The user is not logged in.
  • The user did not register with Google OAuth.
  • The password is missing.
  • The confirmation password is missing.
  • The password is shorter than 10 characters.
  • The password does not include uppercase letters.
  • The password does not include lowercase letters.
  • The password does not include symbols.
  • The password and confirmation password are different.
  • The password cannot be saved to the user's account.

Edge Cases

  • The user sets a password for the first time after registering with Google.
  • The user enters a password with exactly 10 characters.
  • The user enters a password with fewer than 10 characters.
  • The user enters a password with only lowercase letters.
  • The user enters a password with only uppercase letters.
  • The user enters a password without symbols.
  • The user enters a valid new password but a different confirmation password.
  • The user starts setting a password but is no longer logged in.
  • The user already has a password saved.
  • The database update fails while saving the password.
  • The user tries to use email and password sign-in after setting the password.

Success Criteria

This API is successful when:

  • A logged-in Google OAuth user can set a password for their account.
  • Users who are not logged in cannot set a password.
  • Users who did not register with Google OAuth are handled clearly.
  • The password is required.
  • The confirmation password is required.
  • Passwords shorter than 10 characters are rejected.
  • Passwords without uppercase letters are rejected.
  • Passwords without lowercase letters are rejected.
  • Passwords without symbols are rejected.
  • Passwords are rejected when the confirmation password is different.
  • A valid password is saved successfully.
  • The user can use the new password for future email and password sign-ins.
  • The user's Google OAuth access still works after the password is set.
  • Error messages are clear enough for the app to show helpful guidance.

Out Of Scope

  • Registering a new Google OAuth account.
  • Signing in with Google OAuth.
  • Changing an existing password for a normal email and password account.
  • Resetting a forgotten password.
  • Changing the user's email address.
  • Changing the user's name, avatar, projects, or billing data.

Purpose

Create an API that lets a logged-in user add or change their profile avatar.

The avatar should help users make their profile easier to recognize across the product.

User Need

A user needs a simple way to upload a profile picture from their device.

If the user has no avatar yet, the upload should set the first avatar.

If the user already has an avatar, the upload should replace it with the new image.

Expected Experience

When the user opens their profile settings, they should be able to choose an image file and save it as their avatar.

The upload should only work after the user is logged in.

After a successful upload, the user's profile should show the new avatar.

The app should be able to use the saved avatar path when showing the user's profile, account menu, workspace, or other profile areas.

Accepted Avatar Files

The avatar file must be an image.

Accepted image formats are:

  • PNG
  • JPG
  • WebP
  • GIF

The maximum file size is 4 MB.

Files larger than 4 MB should be rejected with a clear message.

Files that are not one of the accepted image formats should be rejected with a clear message.

Storage Behavior

The image file should be stored in object storage.

The database should not store the image file itself.

The database should only store the saved avatar path.

The saved avatar path should be connected to the logged-in user's profile.

Set Or Change Behavior

If the user's avatar profile is empty, the upload should set the avatar path for the first time.

If the user's avatar profile already has a saved path, the upload should change the avatar path to the new image.

After the avatar is changed, the user's profile should use the newest saved avatar path.

Business Rules

  • The user must be logged in before uploading an avatar.
  • Only the logged-in user can set or change their own avatar.
  • The upload must include one image file.
  • The image file must be PNG, JPG, WebP, or GIF.
  • The image file must be 4 MB or smaller.
  • A user can have one active avatar path on their profile.
  • A new successful avatar upload replaces the previous avatar path.
  • The image is stored in object storage.
  • The database stores only the avatar path.
  • The profile API should be able to return the saved avatar path so the app can display it.

Error Cases

The API should return a clear error when:

  • The user is not logged in.
  • No file is uploaded.
  • The uploaded file is not an accepted image format.
  • The uploaded file is larger than 4 MB.
  • The image cannot be saved to object storage.
  • The avatar path cannot be saved to the user's profile.

Edge Cases

  • The user uploads their first avatar.
  • The user changes an existing avatar.
  • The user uploads a PNG image.
  • The user uploads a JPG image.
  • The user uploads a WebP image.
  • The user uploads a GIF image.
  • The user uploads a file larger than 4 MB.
  • The user uploads a file with an unsupported format.
  • The user starts an upload but is no longer logged in.
  • Object storage is temporarily unavailable.
  • The database update fails after the image is uploaded.
  • The user uploads a new avatar soon after uploading another one.

This API is successful when:

  • A logged-in user can upload a profile avatar.

  • Removing an avatar without uploading a replacement.
  • Uploading multiple avatars for one user.

Overview

This task implements a feature allowing an authenticated user to securely change their password by providing their current password and a new password.

Code Implementation

The implementation is separated into the routing, controller, and action layers to ensure clean code architecture.

  1. Routing Setup (src/routes/v1/auth.go):

    • Added the endpoint to the password group: passwordGroup.Post("/change", middleware.Auth(), authController.ChangePassword).
    • The route is strictly gated behind the JWT authentication middleware (middleware.Auth()) to ensure only logged-in users can access it.

  2. Controller Logic (src/controllers/v1/auth/change_password.go):

    • Safely extracts the authenticated user from the context via middleware.GetUser(c).
    • Parses the incoming JSON payload into the ChangePasswordRequest struct.
    • Delegates business logic to the action layer and translates domain-specific errors into standardized HTTP status codes:
      • 401 Unauthorized for an incorrect current password (ErrIncorrectPassword).
      • 400 Bad Request for a short/invalid new password (ErrInvalidNewPassword).

  3. Action & Business Logic (src/action/v1/auth/change_password.go):

    • Enforces a minimum length validation of 8 characters for the new password.
    • Retrieves the user record via GORM using the unique_id.
    • Uses bcrypt.CompareHashAndPassword to cryptographically verify that the provided currentPassword matches the hash currently stored in the database.
    • Upon successful verification, it hashes the new password with bcrypt.GenerateFromPassword and updates the database record.

Security

  • Credential Verification: Forces the user to prove they know the current password before authorizing a change, preventing account takeover if an authenticated session is left open.
  • Secure Hashing: Uses bcrypt for all password comparisons and new password generation to ensure plaintext passwords are never exposed or stored.
  • Session Continuity: Follows the design decision to leave existing JWT sessions active post-change, balancing security with user convenience.

Purpose

Create an API that lets a logged-in user change their current password.

This helps users keep their account secure when they want to replace an old password with a new one.

User Need

A user needs a safe way to change their password while they are signed in.

The user should prove they know the old password before a new password is saved.

The user should also confirm the new password by typing it again, so mistakes are caught before the password is changed.

Expected Experience

When the user opens account security settings, they should be able to change their password.

The user should enter:

  • Old password
  • New password
  • Confirm new password

If the old password is correct, the new password follows the required rules, and the confirmation matches the new password, the password should be changed.

If any of those checks fail, the password change should fail and the old password should stay active.

Password Rules

The new password must be at least 10 characters long.

The new password must include uppercase letters.

The new password must include lowercase letters.

The new password must include symbols.

The user must confirm the new password.

The confirmation password must be the same as the new password.

If the new password and confirmation password are different, the request should be rejected.

Change Behavior

The old password must be checked before the password is changed.

If the old password is different from the user's current password, the password change should fail.

If the new password does not follow the password rules, the password change should fail.

If the confirmation password is different from the new password, the password change should fail.

When the password change fails, the current password should remain unchanged.

When the password change succeeds, the new password should replace the old password.

Business Rules

  • The user must be logged in before changing their password.

Implementation: Stripe Billing Webhook API

Overview

The Webhook API serves as the automated synchronization engine, listening for real-time lifecycle events from Stripe (such as successful payments, renewals, or cancellations) and updating the MapThru database accordingly.

Code Implementation

The implementation is designed for extreme fault tolerance and security.

  1. Cryptographic Validation (src/action/v1/billing/webhook.go):

    • The endpoint intercepts the raw payload body and validates it against the Stripe-Signature header using webhook.ConstructEvent(). This guarantees that the event is genuinely from Stripe and has not been tampered with.

  2. Idempotent Database Operations:

    • When a customer.subscription.created or updated event occurs, the system utilizes a GORM clause.OnConflict (Upsert) mapped to the stripe_subscription_id.
    • This ensures that if Stripe sends duplicate events, or concurrent webhooks fire simultaneously, the database strictly updates the existing record instead of throwing constraint errors or creating duplicate active subscriptions.

  3. Intelligent Timestamp Handling:

    • To support the latest Stripe API versions (e.g., 2025-03-31), the webhook smartly attempts to parse the CurrentPeriodStart. If the data arrives as 0 (due to period properties moving to line items), the system gracefully falls back to the subscription's .Created timestamp.

  4. Infinite Retry Prevention:

    • If the webhook receives an event for a stripe_customer_id that does not exist in the local database, it safely discards the event but returns a successful HTTP 200 acknowledgment. This stops Stripe from aggressively retrying unprocessable payloads and polluting the error logs.

RESULT 02/07/26

✅ Implementation: Database Schema Changes (Billing Feature)

To support payment integration and subscriptions using Stripe, we need to add a few columns to our existing tables to store Stripe reference IDs.

1. users Table

We need to store the user's Stripe Customer ID so we don't create duplicate customers in Stripe when the same user checks out multiple times.

DDL:

ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN stripe_customer_id VARCHAR(255);
CREATE INDEX idx_users_stripe_customer_id ON users(stripe_customer_id);

    StripeCustomerID string `gorm:"type:varchar(255);index" json:"-"`
}

2. subscriptions Table

We need to store the Stripe Subscription ID so that when our webhook receives an update or cancellation event, we can immediately map the payload back to the correct subscription record in our database.

DDL:

ALTER TABLE subscriptions ADD COLUMN stripe_subscription_id VARCHAR(255);
CREATE INDEX idx_subscriptions_stripe_subscription_id ON subscriptions(stripe_subscription_id);

GORM Model Changes (models.go):

    // ... other fields ...
    StripeSubscriptionID string `gorm:"type:varchar(255);index" json:"-"`

Context

Goal

  • Add the necessary columns to store Stripe Customer IDs and Stripe Subscription IDs.
  • Create indexes on these new columns to ensure efficient lookups (like when Webhooks arrive).
  • Generate a DDL script that can be executed to safely apply these changes to the database.
